target_customer: Mobile advertisers and app publishers, with a strong early focus on mobile game developers buying installs
problem: Standard mobile banners were small, intrusive or ignored. Motionlead built transparent animated overlay ads that ran over native and web apps without interrupting navigation.
business_model: Ad technology licensed to publishers who sell their own inventory, plus campaign-based pay per install for game developers

founders.name: Arthur Quérou
founders.background_notes: Described as co-founder and CEO by TechCrunch and Maddyness.

founders.name: Alexei Chemenda
founders.role: Co-founder, later ran the New York gaming office
founders.background_notes: YC page calls him a software engineer who moved to the business side; later CRO and Managing Director Americas at Adikteev.

founders.name: Louis Bur
founders.role: Co-founder, ran the media side from France
founders.background_notes: Named as a co-founder in a 2016 French school alumni interview.

technical_complexity.rationale: Building an overlay ad format that ran on Android, iOS and the web with animation and no navigation interruption needed custom SDK work, but it was standard mobile engineering for a small team.

defensibility.rationale: An ad format is easy for large ad networks or ad SDK vendors to imitate, and the founders later said the licensing model hit its limits by 2015.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: TechCrunch named Google, Facebook and Twitter as dominant mobile advertising players. None copied the format directly in sources found; the company merged with the French ad firm Adikteev in May 2015.

market_need_then: Mobile ad spend was growing fast and game developers were paying roughly 2.50 to 4 dollars per install in 2014 per TechCrunch. The founders said no mobile-native ad format existed, and banner click rates were poor.

branding.brand_signature: First French company accepted into Y Combinator

brand_strength.rationale: Little brand coverage beyond a TechCrunch launch piece and French school and press mentions; the company was folded into Adikteev within two years.

outcome_analysis: Motionlead was an animated mobile ad format company that joined YC in Winter 2014 as the first French startup in the program. It licensed its technology to publishers and sold game install campaigns, but by 2015 the founders said the licensing model had hit its limits, and they joined Adikteev in May 2015 in a deal with no disclosed terms. No outside funding beyond YC was found, so the exit looks like a soft landing for a small team rather than a venture outcome.
notes: Company website motionlead.com did not resolve at fetch time (dead or unreachable). No funding amounts found in any source opened; aggregator listings were not verified. Maddyness calls the deal a merger, YC lists it as acquired and a founder profile says Adikteev acquired it. One aggregator links Motionlead to the Emoteev brand, unconfirmed. No dated competitor list found near the batch; TechCrunch names only large platforms. The exit amount and exact structure are not public. Failure factor is a weak judgment based on the founders' own statement that the licensing model hit its limits.
